name: The Emoticon :-)
summary: A sideways smiling face made of punctuation, invented so people could tell when a message was meant as a joke.

origin.creator: Scott Fahlman
origin.story: On 19 September 1982 Fahlman suggested typing :-) to mark jokes and :-( for serious posts, after a joke on the board was taken seriously.

legacy: Every emoji descends from it.

name: Godwin's Law
summary: As an online discussion grows longer, the chance that someone compares someone else to Hitler approaches one.

origin.creator: Mike Godwin
origin.story: Godwin put forward the 'law' in 1990 as a way to point out how quickly Usenet arguments escalated.

legacy: One of the first laws of online behavior, still quoted in comment sections.

name: Spam
summary: Unwanted bulk messages, named after a sketch about a café where every dish includes Spam.

origin.story: Named after a Monty Python sketch where a chorus drowns out everything with 'Spam'. MUD users used the word for flooding first, and a 1994 Usenet ad posted to thousands of groups made it famous.

legacy: The joke became the technical term.

name: The Good Times Virus
summary: A fake virus warning that copied itself better than any real virus, because people kept forwarding it.
quote: FORWARD THIS TO EVERYONE YOU KNOW

origin.story: In late 1994 warnings spread by email that opening a message titled 'Good Times' would wipe your hard drive. The virus never existed. The warning was the thing that spread.

legacy: The ancestor of every chain message.

name: The Dancing Baby
summary: A rendered 3D baby doing a cha-cha, and probably the first viral video.

origin.creator: Michael Girard & Robert Lurye
origin.story: A 3D sample animation made for Autodesk Character Studio got passed around as a file attachment, then shown on Ally McBeal in 1998.

legacy: Showed that a looping animation could travel the world on its own.

name: The Hampster Dance
summary: A web page that was nothing but dancing hamster GIFs and a squeaky song. Millions of people visited.

origin.creator: Deidre LaCarte
origin.story: A homepage covered in rows of animated hamster GIFs, played over a sped-up sample from Disney's Robin Hood (1973).

legacy: The original attention economy, built from four GIFs.

name: I KISS YOU!!!
summary: A sincere personal homepage that the whole internet came to visit.
quote: WELCOME TO MY HOMEPAGE!!!!!!!!! I KISS YOU!!!!!

origin.creator: Mahir Çağrı
origin.story: A Turkish journalist's earnest homepage, with its broken-English greeting and invitations to visit, was linked everywhere.

legacy: An early lesson in going viral without meaning to.

name: All Your Base Are Belong to Us
summary: A mistranslated villain's line from a 1989 shoot-'em-up that turned into the web's catchphrase.
quote: ALL YOUR BASE ARE BELONG TO US

origin.story: A badly translated cutscene from the 1991 European release of Zero Wing got passed around forums, then became a 2001 Flash video set to a techno track.

legacy: Engrish turned into a way of belonging.

links.why: Nonsense lore that a generation took completely seriously.

name: Peanut Butter Jelly Time
summary: A dancing banana. That's the whole thing.

origin.story: A pixelated banana dances to the Buckwheat Boyz song in a loop.

legacy: Hall of fame for nonsense loops.

name: Badger Badger Badger
summary: An endless chant of badgers, mushrooms and one snake.

origin.creator: Jonti Picking
origin.story: A hypnotic Flash loop of badgers doing calisthenics, broken up by a mushroom and a snake.

legacy: The peak of Flash-era repetition.

name: Star Wars Kid
summary: One of the first viral videos, and one of the first public conversations about cyberbullying.

origin.story: Classmates uploaded a teenager's private video of himself swinging a golf ball retriever like a lightsaber, without his consent.

legacy: A reminder that there's a real person on the other side.

links.why: Home video that escaped the home.

name: Numa Numa
summary: A man in headphones lip-syncing a Moldovan pop song with his whole heart.

origin.creator: Gary Brolsma
origin.story: Brolsma lip-synced at his webcam to O-Zone's 'Dragostea Din Tei' with total commitment, and posted it in December 2004.

legacy: Set the template for webcam performance culture.

name: Leeroy Jenkins
summary: A battle cry for ruining a carefully laid plan.

origin.creator: Ben Schulz
origin.story: In a World of Warcraft raid video, a guild spends ages planning, and then one player charges in yelling his own name.

legacy: Shouted before every reckless decision since.

name: Chuck Norris Facts
summary: Over-the-top 'facts' about the toughest man alive.
quote: Chuck Norris counted to infinity. Twice.

origin.creator: Ian Spector
origin.story: Absurd claims about Chuck Norris's power spread from a 2005 generator site.

legacy: A joke format that never really ended.

name: LOLcats
summary: Cat photos captioned in broken baby talk.

origin.story: 4chan's 'Caturday' cat pictures with captions became a whole website in 2007, along with a whole dialect.

legacy: Showed that the internet runs on cats.

links.why: Cats with captions became cats with careers.

name: Rickrolling
summary: A disguised link that sends you to Rick Astley.

origin.story: It grew out of the 'duckroll' prank: a link promises one thing and plays Rick Astley's 1987 'Never Gonna Give You Up' instead.

legacy: The prank that never dies, and Astley embraced it.

links.why: The bait-and-switch, and the grin that goes with it.

name: Charlie Bit My Finger
summary: A baby bites his big brother's finger, and the brother's reaction became famous.

origin.creator: Howard Davies-Carr
origin.story: A home video of two brothers, uploaded for family, became one of YouTube's most-watched clips.

legacy: The golden age of the accidental home video.

name: Dramatic Chipmunk
summary: A rodent turns, stares and gets a dramatic chord.

origin.story: A five-second clip from Japanese TV of a prairie dog (not a chipmunk) turning to the camera, set to a dramatic sting.

legacy: The shortest drama ever filmed.

name: Rage Comics
summary: Crudely drawn faces for every emotion, in comic-strip form.

origin.story: A four-panel MS Paint comic ending in a 'FFFFUUUU' face started an entire cast of faces: Forever Alone, Me Gusta, Y U NO.

legacy: A shared emotional vocabulary, before emoji.

name: Trollface
summary: The grin of someone who is messing with you, and knows it.

origin.creator: Carlos Ramirez
origin.story: Drawn in MS Paint and posted to DeviantArt, the grin became shorthand for trolling.

legacy: The face of an entire era of internet behavior.

name: Keyboard Cat
summary: A cat in a shirt who plays you off stage.

origin.creator: Charlie Schmidt
origin.story: Schmidt filmed his cat 'playing' a keyboard in 1984. In 2009 people started tacking it onto the end of fail videos.

legacy: The internet's exit music.

name: Double Rainbow
summary: A man so overjoyed by a double rainbow that he can barely speak.

origin.creator: Paul Vasquez
origin.story: Vasquez filmed a double rainbow near Yosemite and was completely overcome. The video took off in 2010.

legacy: The purest wonder the internet has recorded.

name: Trololo
summary: A Soviet baritone sings a wordless song with a smile you can't shake.

origin.creator: Eduard Khil
origin.story: Khil's grinning 1976 performance of a wordless Soviet song came back 34 years later.

legacy: Proved the internet can bring back anything.

name: Nyan Cat
summary: A pixel cat with a Pop-Tart body, flying through space trailing a rainbow.

origin.creator: Chris Torres
origin.story: Torres's pixel-art Pop-Tart cat was paired with a vocaloid song on YouTube in April 2011.

legacy: Pixel nostalgia, looped forever.

links.why: A looping animal GIF and a squeaky song, twelve years apart.

name: Planking
summary: Lying stiff as a board somewhere unexpected.

origin.story: People lay rigid and face-down in unlikely places and shared the photos. It spread fastest in Australia.

legacy: The template for every photo fad after it.

name: Gangnam Style
summary: A K-pop horse-riding dance that the whole planet learned.

origin.creator: PSY
origin.story: In December 2012 PSY's music video became the first YouTube video to pass a billion views.

legacy: Pushed YouTube's view counter past its limits.

name: Grumpy Cat
summary: A cat who looked deeply unimpressed by everything.

origin.story: A photo of Tardar Sauce, whose underbite made her look permanently unimpressed, went up on Reddit in 2012.

legacy: A cat who became a celebrity. She died in 2019.

links.why: The unimpressed cat returns as a reaction image.

name: Doge
summary: A Shiba Inu thinking in broken, multicolored Comic Sans.
quote: such wow. very meme. much archive.

origin.creator: Atsuko Sato (photo)
origin.story: A 2010 photo of a Shiba Inu named Kabosu, surrounded by Comic Sans inner monologue. It inspired Dogecoin.

legacy: It turned into a currency. Kabosu died in 2024.

links.why: An animal the whole internet adopted.

name: Harlem Shake
summary: A masked dancer alone, then sudden chaos.

origin.story: A 30-second format set to Baauer's track: one person dances alone, then the bass drops and the whole room is in costume.

legacy: The first truly global participatory video format.

links.why: Everyone doing the same silly thing, then posting it.

name: Ice Bucket Challenge
summary: A dare that raised over a hundred million dollars for charity.

origin.story: People poured ice water over their heads, tagged friends to do the same and donated to ALS research.

legacy: It funded real research.

name: The Dress
summary: A dress that people saw as different colors.
quote: Blue and black or white and gold?

origin.story: A washed-out photo of a dress split the world: blue and black, or white and gold? (It was blue and black.)

legacy: Even scientists studied it.

name: Damn Daniel
summary: Being hyped up by a friend, one outfit at a time.
quote: Damn, Daniel! Back at it again with the white Vans!

origin.creator: Josh Holz
origin.story: A string of Snapchat clips of a friend praising Daniel's outfit, especially his white Vans.

legacy: A Snapchat-era catchphrase.

name: Harambe
summary: A real loss that the internet mourned, mostly through absurdity.

origin.story: A gorilla was killed at the Cincinnati Zoo after a child fell into his enclosure. The grief online turned into a strange collective memorial.

legacy: Shows how the internet processes grief.

name: Distracted Boyfriend
summary: A stock photo template for being drawn to the wrong thing.

origin.creator: Antonio Guillem
origin.story: A 2015 stock photo of a man turning to look at another woman while his girlfriend glares. People started labeling it in 2017.

legacy: Stock photos turned out to be meme gold.

name: Tide Pods
summary: Laundry pods that looked like candy.

origin.story: Jokes about how tempting laundry pods looked grew into a 'challenge' that prompted public safety warnings.

legacy: A joke that got out of hand.

name: Woman Yelling at a Cat
summary: Two unrelated photos that turned into a perfect argument.

origin.story: A reality TV scene of a woman shouting was put next to a photo of a white cat named Smudge sitting at a dinner table, looking confused.

legacy: Mashups of unrelated pictures as a form.

name: Storm Area 51
summary: A joke raid on a secret base that almost happened.
quote: They can't stop all of us.

origin.creator: Matty Roberts
origin.story: A joke Facebook event to raid Area 51 on 20 September 2019 got about two million RSVPs, plus a plan to 'Naruto run' past the bullets.

legacy: A joke that drew a real crowd.

name: OK Boomer
summary: Two words that end the argument.

origin.story: A dismissive two-word reply to older generations spread on TikTok and eventually got said out loud in parliament.

legacy: A generation gap in two words.

name: Coffin Dance
summary: Pallbearers who dance with the casket.

origin.creator: Ghanaian pallbearers
origin.story: Dancing Ghanaian pallbearers, set to the EDM track 'Astronomia', became gallows humor during the 2020 pandemic.

legacy: Grief and joy carried together.

name: Sus
summary: One crewmate is not what they seem.

origin.story: During lockdown everyone played a deduction game about spotting the impostor, and the slang stuck.

legacy: The word 'sus' made it into everyday speech.

name: Bernie's Mittens
summary: One cozy man, cut out and dropped into history.

origin.creator: Brendan Smialowski (photo)
origin.story: A photo of a senator sitting cross-legged in a parka and handmade mittens at the 2021 US inauguration got pasted into every scene imaginable.

legacy: The cut-out paste meme at its peak.

name: Skibidi Toilet
summary: Heads singing from toilets, waging an endless war.

origin.creator: Alexey Gerasimov
origin.story: A Source Filmmaker series about singing heads in toilets at war with camera-headed people grew into an epic with billions of views.

legacy: A new generation's mythology.

name: Barbenheimer
summary: A pink doll movie and an atomic bomb movie, watched as a double bill.

origin.story: Two very different films came out on the same day, 21 July 2023, and the internet made them a double feature.

legacy: The internet booked people into cinemas.

name: Moo Deng
summary: A tiny, furious baby hippo.

origin.creator: Khao Kheow Open Zoo
origin.story: A baby pygmy hippo born in Thailand in July 2024 became famous for slippery, bitey tantrums.

legacy: A small creature everyone adored.

name: Brain Rot
summary: What endless scrolling does to your mind, and the content that does it.

origin.story: Oxford named it Word of the Year for 2024, though Thoreau used the phrase back in 1854.

legacy: The internet naming its own condition.

links.why: Hypnotic nonsense loops were brainrot before the word existed.

name: Italian Brainrot
summary: A whole pantheon of AI-generated nonsense creatures.

origin.story: AI-generated absurd creatures with fake-Italian names and lore: a shark in sneakers, a crocodile bomber plane, a wooden log with a bat.

legacy: The first meme mythology built with generative AI.

links.why: Computer-generated creatures going viral, three decades apart.

summary: Two numbers and a shrug, and nobody can say what they mean.

origin.story: From the song 'Doot Doot (6 7)' and basketball edits, kids started shouting the numbers along with a palms-up shrug, for no clear reason.

legacy: Meaning dissolving in real time.
